info.bio:
Soft Cell es un dúo británico exponentes del synth-pop (a veces también llamado techno-pop) de la década de los ochenta. 
Formado por, Marc Almond (Peter Marc Sinclair Almond), nacido el 9 de julio de 1959 en Southport Inglaterra en la voz. 
Dave Ball, nacido el 3 de Mayo de 1959, en los sintetizadores. 
El dúo se formó en la ciudad de Leeds, Inglaterra, en octubre de 1979 por Marc y Dave, estudiantes de arte, produciendo música para representaciones teatrales.

scenes.name: Synthpop británico
scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
scenes.desc: Con The Human League a la cabeza, el auge de 1981-1982: los sintetizadores baratos (el Wasp), las cajas de ritmos Linn y las baterías Simmons democratizan la electrónica, al punto de que el sindicato de músicos propone racionarlos. Instrumento andrógino frente a la guitarra fálica, refugio para los adolescentes que se sentían distintos. Soft Cell lleva la sordidez neoyorquina de Suicide a Leeds («Tainted Love», «Bedsitter», Non-Stop Erotic Cabaret); Japan, máscaras de dandi de Catford, pasa del glam desfasado a la belleza escultural de «Ghosts»; OMD, Pete Shelley («Homosapien»), y Depeche Mode, de chicos inocentes de Basildon en Mute a la política y el sadomasoquismo de «Everything Counts» y «Master and Servant». Hacia 1983 el diluvio de grupos mediocres provoca la reacción y vuelven las guitarras.

podcast.title: Duo Formation and Initial Breakup (1978-1984)
podcast.body: Soft Cell was a two-piece British technopop band that existed from 1978 to 1984. Mark Almond and David Ball amicably decided to part ways without drama or fights, feeling "it was just time" after releasing a farewell album and conducting a tour. "Soft Cell, the two-piece British technopop band that lasted from 1978 to 1984 before Mark Ommendon David Ball, amically decided to part ways."

podcast.title: Reunion for Nightclub Opening (2001)
podcast.body: The duo reunited on February 1, 2001, to mark the grand opening of a London nightclub named Ocean, after an interval of 17 years, eight months, and one day since their breakup. "On February 1st, 2001, they just gave up and announced a reunion to mark the grand opening of a nightclub in London called Ocean."

podcast.title: Mark Almond Motorcycle Accident (2005)
podcast.body: On October 17, 2005, Mark Almond was a passenger in a motorcycle crash that resulted in serious injuries, multiple operations, rehabilitation, and even counseling for mental trauma, though he has since recovered. "There was a scare on October 17th, 2005 when Mark was a passenger on a motorcycle. There was a crash, some serious injuries, operations, rehab and even counseling for the mental trauma."

podcast.title: Dave Ball Death (2025) – Performed in Wheelchair, Completed Final Album Before Death
podcast.body: Dave Ball, one half of British synth-pop duo Soft Cell, died in 2025. His final years were marked by severe health problems that forced him to perform from a wheelchair. He died shortly after completing a final album with the group. "Died shortly after completing a final album with the group."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Breakup Reason - Tainted Love's Shadow
podcast.body: The immense success of "Tainted Love" became a burden, overshadowing all their other creative efforts and ultimately leading them to "give up" rather than continuously fight against its dominance. "It was such a big hit that it overshadowed everything else they tried to do. So rather than fight it, they just gave up."

"They played all the groups that we've talked about in many more. Eurythmics, XTC, Soft Sale, Adamance, Human League, Bowah Wow, and The Go Go's..."

podcast.body: Soft Cell, an early 80s techno pop act, is identified as having been influenced by Kraftwerk, demonstrating the German band's widespread reach in shaping the electronic music landscape. "Early 80s techno pop like OMD and Soft Cell. Craftwork."

podcast.body: Part of the wave of "fun, fresh music" from the UK that became popular in North America due to exposure on MTV in its early days. "There was Durand Durant and the Human League and Blomage and the Thompson Twins and Soft Cell."

podcast.body: Soft Cell (referred to as "Soft-Sale") is identified as a band that emerged from the New Romantic movement, directly influenced by the legacy of glam rock, particularly David Bowie and Roxy Music. "Soft-Sale."

podcast.title: Only US Hit
podcast.body: "Tainted Love" (1981) was Soft Cell's sole US hit, an obscure 1964 Northern Soul B-side they transformed into a synth-pop classic, reaching number eight on the Hot 100 in 1982. "Soft Cell's only US hit."

podcast.title: Post-Breakup Careers and Continued Contact
podcast.body: After their initial breakup, both Mark Almond and Dave Ball pursued solo careers, staying in close contact over the years, though neither achieved the level of success that "Tainted Love" had. "Both Mark Ommendon and Dave Ball stayed in close touch over the years as each worked on solo careers. Nothing, of course, though they ever did, ever matched Tainted Love."

podcast.title: Prominent Technopop Band
podcast.body: Soft Cell was recognized as one of the bands contributing to the commercial peak of Technopop in the early 1980s, further expanding the genre's accessibility and popularity. "They were joined by bands like Durant, Rand, Soft Cell, OMD, ABC, DePesh Mode, Oflaca Seagulls, Men Without Hats, and so many others."

podcast.title: Reunion Concert
podcast.body: Soft Cell is currently experiencing renewed popularity due to an upcoming reunion concert, their first together in many years. Mark Almond has announced his return specifically for this performance, a factor that is likely being leveraged by this re-edition. "ahora finales este año van a dar su primer concierto juntos en mil años, desde que Mark Almond ha dicho que va a volver con un software para dar solo este concierto."

xref.title: Influential After 1977
xref.body: Kraftwerk is considered by some to be the most influential band in the world next to The Beatles, with their impact traceable in music starting anytime after 1977. Their influence spans EDM, techno (including Detroit techno and Daft Punk), ambient and chillout music, synth and sample-constructed music (like Simple Minds and Depeche Mode), early 80s techno pop (OMD, Soft Cell), and industrial music (Nine Inch Nails). "Pick any starting point in music anytime after 1977. And you will somehow be led back in some fashion to Craftwork."

xref.title: Feminization of Male Rock Stars
xref.body: Bowie was the first to openly and unabashedly feminize the macho male rock and roll star. His pioneering embrace of androgyny led to a subsequent wave of acts that were androgynous, bisexual, gay, or "plain femme looking," including artists like Depeche Mode, Gary Numan, Soft Cell, and Eurythmics. "Bowie was the first to unabashedly and openly feminize the macho male rock and roll star."
